title: Reuse one exported help UI dependency with per-app themes
description:
Design-only planning requested by Ryan during voice. Implementation remains unstarted; no code, infrastructure, deployment, purchase or publishing authorization is implied. Initial status stays open (Discovery), unassigned.

As a product integrator, I want a shared exported Papyrus wiki/help UI dependency, so that each product embeds consistent help without maintaining a bespoke implementation.

Acceptance behavior (planned, not executable or verified yet):
```gherkin
Feature: Reuse one exported help UI dependency with per-app themes
  Scenario: Embed Help in two products
    Given two applications use the shared exported help UI dependency
    When each configures its own theme, navigation entry and authorized documentation binding
    Then both receive common wiki/help behavior from that dependency
    And each retains its product typography, colors and appropriate application chrome
    And content scope and access checks do not change with theme selection
  Scenario: Upgrade shared behavior
    Given a reviewed shared help UI version is adopted by a consumer
    When that consumer upgrades
    Then its documented integration contract and theme hooks allow behavior to be verified without copying a separate help implementation
```

Package export/API, supported host environments, CSS isolation, accessibility, framework constraints and release/version policy remain boundary decisions. Reuse existing Papyrus/Markus and Chatticus mechanisms where suitable. A shared dependency is required direction; a new repo or specific package name is not approved.
